scope: Manual spot review of exact NASA NTRS text blobs currently stored in data/datasets/candidates/nasa-ntrs-public-use/documents/. This is a file-level content/metadata audit, not global corpus admission.
method: Fetched each exact text blob from main and recorded its Git blob SHA-1 and byte size.
Compared document ID, title, author and public distribution/copyright metadata with the corresponding official NASA NTRS record.
Inspected OCR text at the beginning and representative interior sections for legibility, extraction corruption and obvious scan artefacts.
Did not infer rights from NASA authorship alone; used the record-specific NTRS Copyright and Distribution Limits fields.

verified_metadata.title: Paraglider Recovery Systems
verified_metadata.author: Francis M. Rogallo
verified_metadata.copyright: Work of the US Gov. Public Use Permitted.

decisions.reason: The body is coherent and technically readable across inspected sections; minor OCR and layout artefacts remain, especially around figures and page transitions.

verified_metadata.title: Development of Design Strength Levels for the Elastic Stability of Monocoque Cones Under Axial Compression

decisions.reason: Title and technical subject match the official NTRS record. The discussion and statistical engineering prose are readable, with column-order and OCR errors that should be retained as extraction caveats.

decisions.reason: The source is relevant and rights metadata is positive, but representative body text contains frequent character substitutions, broken words and line/column corruption (for example, mangled units and technical terms). Re-extract or repair before training.

verified_metadata.title: High Energy Propellants: A Continuing Bibliography
verified_metadata.author: NASA Continuing Bibliography Program (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)
verified_metadata.copyright: Work of the US Gov. Public Use Permitted.

decisions.reason: Title page, introduction, bibliography entries and later section sampled. The document is a coherent annotated bibliography of unclassified reports and journal articles; OCR splits letters and has local recognition errors but structure and technical references remain readable. NASA's individual record confirms public distribution and US Government public-use status.

verified_metadata.author: Prepared by Goddard Space Flight Center
verified_metadata.copyright: Work of the US Gov. Public Use Permitted.

decisions.reason: NASA individual record confirms NASA-SP-30, public distribution and US Government public-use status. Sampled title/foreword, body passages at multiple offsets and later technical sections. OCR has local character substitutions and damaged figures/tables, but the main prose is coherent and technically readable.

source_level_findings.finding: Author metadata includes apparent address fragments ('Escondido Rd', 'Stan 412') among author names.
Author list contains malformed fragment '| Ran'; attribution metadata needs source reconciliation.
The record concerns online developmental research but is routed to philosophy_general; domain assignment is not supported by the title/subject and needs correction.

aggregate.pack_verification: 824/824 packed document SHA-256 and byte-length checks pass; 824/824 item-level NASA rights allowlist checks pass; zero exact duplicate texts within NASA candidate pack. This is pack-local only; cross-source exact/near-duplicate checks remain pending.

limitations: Git blob SHA-1 values identify the exact repository blobs; they are not represented as document SHA-256 values.
The 2 NASA content passes remain candidates until exact-payload hash checks, global exact/near-duplicate checks, current redistribution recheck, and partition isolation pass.
ScienceVerse compressed document payloads were not decoded in this review; its listed findings are metadata-only and do not constitute content approval.
This review does not promote any document to admitted or training_eligible.

pack_verification.scope_note: Checks were independently rerun over the downloaded workflow artifact ZIP and all 824 decompressed JSONL rows. Exact deduplication here covers the NASA pack only, not other source corpora.
